name: kiss-cut
title: Kiss Cut
description: A marquee built from a subtraction: a rotary die kiss-cuts labels into a laminate web's face stock only, and a stripping bar continuously peels the waste matrix off the liner at a fixed 38 degree angle onto a growing rewind spool — the label never moves, the waste around it does, leaving a continuous unbroken liner behind.
useWhen: a marquee/logo-ribbon surface whose identity is a subtraction — content that stays behind while the material around it is continuously removed — pick this over marquee-ticker-glyph (a scrub instrument you drag through text at speed) or ticker-tape-splice (a live feed of chips streaming in and pruning off the left edge); both of those are content ADDED into a moving stream, while kiss-cut's marks are fixed to the liner and only the waste around them travels.
instruction: Build `<KissCut paused? onPausedChange? className? />` as a card-scale 2D canvas band (default aspect-ratio 3/1, geometry derived from `M = min(bandW, bandH)`, `W = bandW`) modelling rotary die-cutting of pressure-sensitive labels. LAYOUT (worked at W=3*M, M=340px): web speed `v = 0.40*W px/s` right-to-left; label width `0.13*M`, height assumed `0.10*M` (the one number the spec leaves open), matrix gutter `0.022*M` between labels, matrix margin `0.028*M` top/bottom, corner radius `0.018*M` (a square corner would tear the matrix — factually required, not decorative); a rotary die (diameter `0.13*M`) sits far right, its angular speed `v / dieRadius` so surface speed always matches the web, with 3 tick marks per revolution; a stripping bar at `x = 0.62*W`; a rewind spool at a FIXED 38 degree strip angle up-and-right of the strip bar (its position is DERIVED from that angle and the canvas bounds, clamped so its max radius clears the top/right edges, never placed independently and aimed at — an earlier build's ribbon shot off-canvas doing that), radius growing `0.045*M -> 0.11*M` over 40s then doffing (easing back to the start radius) over a final 700ms. READ ORDER, LEFT TO RIGHT ON SCREEN: bare siliconised liner in the gutters (matrix already stripped) -> the strip bar and the peeling matrix ribbon -> intact matrix in the gutters (cut but not yet peeled) -> a partial-reveal zone under the die -> an uncut, unscored sheet at the right edge. ONE CONTINUOUS LINER BAND underlies the FULL canvas width, drawn once, unbroken — the physical proof the die went through the face stock and not the liner; face-stock label/gutter rects are drawn on top of it and only withheld where the matrix has actually been carried away. THE KISS-CUT SCORE LINE IS CARRIED IN VALUE, NEVER IN `--border`: a groove stroke (face stock mixed 32% toward this theme's darker anchor) plus an adjacent lit shoulder stroke (mixed 32% toward the lighter anchor), fading in via `globalAlpha` proportional to how far a label's left edge has passed the die (`clamp((dieX - labelLeft)/labelW, 0,1)`) so the die visibly stamps each cut rather than the whole sheet snapping pre-scored. `--border` is reserved for the band's own top/bottom framing hairline only. NECKING IS GEOMETRY-ONLY: the peel ribbon's cross-width narrows by `neckFrac` (6% normal, 10% below `M=200px`) as a `bump()` function of a label's leading edge nearing the strip bar (2.5s spacing at the worked scale), PLUS a further 9% for 620ms once per a 9.3s tension-hunt sine's peak — additive, clamped, and it is a POLYGON WIDTH change only, never a colour or luminance flash. TWO-CLOCK, SCREEN-VS-MATERIAL SEPARATION: labels, score lines and marks scroll in material space (`labelScreenX = k*unitPeriod - scrollX - phaseOffset`); the peel ribbon's Lambert gradient (a 4-stop gradient from an underside tone through a dark and a light face-stock mix, spanning roughly 0.26 of the value range) and a bare-liner gloss sheen are anchored to FIXED canvas coordinates that never move with `scrollX` — a still lamp over moving material, which is what keeps the already-peeled region (left of the strip bar) from reading as a static frame sliding sideways under a crop comparison. `phaseOffset` is chosen every layout pass so a label's leading edge sits exactly on the strip bar at `STATIC_TIME`, making the reduced-motion frame's described state (peel front at a corner, matrix necked to its minimum) exact rather than incidental. A MATRIX BREAK fires every 47s: the free end whips off the fixed-angle line over 260ms while the web decelerates to 0 over 900ms (`speedMul` eased 1->0), the ribbon is entirely absent while stopped, then a fresh ribbon regrows over 700ms as the web ramps back to `v` over 1.1s — `scrollX`/`dieAngle` integrate `v * speedMul` every frame, so the drift and recovery are visible, not a jump cut; `simT` (elapsed unpaused time, driving the break/tension/spool cycles) keeps advancing independent of `speedMul`. MARKS: 7 seeded abstract placeholder marks (5 below `M=200px`), five deterministic stroke templates keyed by each cell's material-space index `k mod markCount` (never per-frame random, never real logos/wordmarks) drawn at `--foreground` 0.78 alpha, printed on the face stock independent of cut/peel state. TOKENS: `--background`, `--foreground`, `--ns-muted` (hardware — the die, strip bar and spool, kept visually distinct from the material tones), `--border` (frame only) are read as hex via `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`, parsed to RGB (no CSS color-mix reliance), and every derived tone (liner, bare liner, face stock, score groove/shoulder, ribbon light/dark, underside) is a linear RGB mix toward whichever of bg/fg is this theme's lighter or darker anchor — never a literal white/black. `--ns-accent` never touches the canvas; it is only the pause button's `focus-visible` ring. NOTHING PAINTS before the first successful token read on all three paths (rAF start, ResizeObserver fire, IntersectionObserver resume) — `boot()` retries on rAF until tokens resolve. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` renders exactly one composed frame at `STATIC_TIME = 2.32s`, computed in closed form (`scrollX = v*STATIC_TIME`, `dieAngle = (v/dieRadius)*STATIC_TIME`, spool radius from the same 40s/700ms formula) since no break has fired by then — byte-stable, re-derived identically on ResizeObserver and the theme MutationObserver. DPR capped at 2 (card-scale, not full-bleed); ResizeObserver on the host element; IntersectionObserver pauses the rAF loop off-screen. A real `<button aria-pressed>` (copying ticker-tape-splice's pattern) offers an explicit WCAG 2.2.2 stop for motion running past 5s — pausing freezes the simulation clock but keeps polling rAF so unpausing resumes instantly. Zero dependencies, Canvas 2D only, no WebGL.
